evidence: Receiving DO2 at 52 h = 9.92 mg/L (minimum constraint 2.0 mg/L; large margin)
Receiving P assays: 0.022 g/L @24h, 1.074 @36h, 2.943 @48h — monotonic, healthy ramp
Source batches 1-3 P at same time points: ~0-0.03, 1.02-1.12, 2.98-3.06 g/L; peaks ~8.1-8.4 g/L at 72-84h
Receiving DO2 dip to ~7.4-8.4 mg/L at 24-28 h matches source pattern and recovers fully
No evidence of overfeeding or oxygen limitation that would justify feed reduction or aeration increase
submission.rationale: The receiving fermentation matches the healthy source-batch ensemble at every observable point: P at 36 h (1.074 g/L) and 48 h (2.943 g/L) fall inside the source range, and DO2 (9.9 mg/L at 52 h) is far above the 2.0 mg/L minimum with the same transient dip-and-recovery pattern seen in all three sources. Feed reduction or a stop would sacrifice product mass during the 52-84 h window where sources gain ~5 g/L; increasing air adds nothing when DO is already non-limiting. KEEP preserves the projected trajectory toward the ~8 g/L source-class peak.
submission.uncertainty: Receiving hidden parameters may differ from sources; only delayed P assays through 48 h are available (next assay at 56 h would confirm the ~5.4-5.5 g/L region). Source trajectories decline slightly after 72-84 h, so optimal harvest timing matters but is outside the intervention menu. Confidence in KEEP is high since no observable deviates from the healthy ensemble.

evidence: Receiving DO2 52h = 9.92 mg/L vs source-1/2/3 at 52h of ~10.7-11.5 mg/L (receiving observations vs source-1/2/3 observations at time_h=52)
Source batches: P peaks ~8.0-8.4 g/L at 72h then declines to ~6.4-7.0 g/L at 96h while DO sags to 7.4-8.2 mg/L (delayed assays at 76h and 100h)
Forward model: keep 576.3 kg / min DO 6.74; reduce_feed 595.5 kg / min DO 7.56; combined 595.5 kg / min DO 8.01 (all feasible, min DO well above 2.0 limit)
Combined sensitivity: 590-602 kg, min DO 6.6-9.1 mg/L — all 5 members feasible
submission.rationale: Receiving DO tracks below source batches and source data show late-phase DO sag with product decline under continued feeding. Combined (feed x0.8, air x1.15) yields the same predicted mass gain as reduce_feed (~595.5 kg vs 576.3 kg under keep) with a higher DO floor (8.0 vs 7.6 mg/L), giving margin against the receiving line's tighter oxygen trajectory and parameter uncertainty. All sensitivity members remain feasible; oxygen constraint never approached.
submission.uncertainty: Forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect for the receiving process; hidden receiving parameters (transfer multiplier 0.86 estimated) could shift outcomes. Product mass difference between reduce_feed and combined is within model noise, so the choice hinges on DO margin; if the receiving oxygen transfer is better than estimated, reduce_feed alone would suffice. Assay clocks (4h turnaround) mean the next product confirmation arrives after further DO decline.
